intro: Welcome to Kibyra, known as the 'City of Gladiators', an ancient city in Burdur province. Its story runs from the 2nd century BC to the 6th century AD. Two things made it famous: the world-renowned Medusa mosaic in its odeon, and its gladiator school.
history: According to Strabo, Kibyra was founded by Lydians who migrated to the Kabalis region, and with its neighbours it formed the 'Tetrapolis', a league of four cities. Then, in AD 23, an earthquake destroyed it. The city was rebuilt with the aid of Emperor Tiberius and, in gratitude, took a new name: 'Caesarea Kibyra'. Under Rome it became a centre of justice and trade, famous for its gladiator school.
structure-1: You are now at the Medusa Mosaic Odeon. This is the odeon whose floor bears a Medusa mosaic, the treasure that made Kibyra famous.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the stadium, the theatre, the agora and the Roman baths.
facts: Did you know? The Medusa mosaic at Kibyra is the only known depiction of Medusa made in the 'opus sectile' technique, and for most of the year it is protected under cover. The rock-cut stadium seats ten thousand, its rows carved straight out of the hillside. And the city was known for training gladiators and breeding horses; ancient sources praise the Kibyran cavalry.
outro: This brings our tour of Kibyra to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
